chosen.title: woman taking in the ocean view from her hotel room
chosen.faces: none - back-view silhouette only; face never visible
chosen.why: Dark interior, back view. A thin slit of light at 1.6s, the figure pushes the double door open at ~2.0-2.2s and the frame floods to near-white by 3.0s, then holds as a silhouette with arms on the door frames until 4.3s. Exactly the 'light pours through the door gap and blows the frame out' beat; low saturation, natural light, no text/logo. Cut 1.6-4.3s; do not extend past ~4.4s (subject is in a t-shirt and underwear, which becomes readable once lit, and a palm leaf enters the top of frame).

alternates.why: POV-ish white door with a hanging key; handle turns ~2.0s and the door cracks open ~2.3s. But it opens onto a bedroom (no light bloom) and a saturated yellow/blue dress fills the gap from ~2.5s, so only 0-2.7s is usable. 720p.

Muted grey exterior; front door opens at ~2.5s and a woman steps out at ~3s. Camera is outside (not POV/back view), her face is frontal 3.0-4.5s, and there is no light bloom. Fallback only if a literal 'leaving the house' shot is preferred. 720p.

notes: Searches: 'opening door to bright light' and 'door sunlight' returned 0 results; 'leaving home' returned nothing relevant. Useful hits came from 'opening door', 'door', 'walking out door', 'front door'. Rejected: 256 (elevator, smiling face at tablet, stock-ad feel), 21813 (frontal face), 314/8733 (not downloaded; corporate glass-door exit and family entering with faces). Chosen clip is a hotel balcony onto the sea rather than a street, but between 1.6-4.3s the view is mostly blown-out sky/sea, so the read is 'dark room -> door -> white light'. Use a 16:9 frame as is; consider a slight push-in or a 1-2% brightness lift at the tail to strengthen the white-out.
